claims.text: The nanoparticles are sub-10 nm equiatomic Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt particles.
The as-fabricated nanoparticles are initially a metastable solid solution.
Bulk high-entropy-alloy models associate high configurational entropy and lattice distortion with sluggish diffusion and thermal stabilization.
Bulk TiCoCrFeMn has a diffusion coefficient of approximately 10^-19 m^2/s at 1000 °C.
Heating is performed in vacuum from room temperature to 1000 K.
Above 600 K, surface-energy-driven processes override sluggish diffusion in sub-10 nm Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles.
The nanoparticles' high surface-to-volume ratio makes surface-energy terms dominant over bulk stabilization.
Surface diffusion pathways bypass diffusion barriers associated with bulk lattice distortion.
High nanoparticle surface energy lowers the activation barrier for surface diffusion and segregation.
Enhanced surface diffusion causes rapid elemental segregation and phase separation.
Surface-mediated rearrangement and Ostwald ripening proceed faster than bulk sluggish diffusion.
The higher chemical potential of smaller particles drives mass transport from small particles to larger particles.
Volatilization of components such as Cu, Au, or Co may contribute to the loss of the smallest particles at high temperature in vacuum.
Heating will produce distinct elemental or binary-rich domains.
Ostwald ripening will shift the particle-size distribution toward larger particle sizes.
Heating will significantly reduce the number of sub-5 nm particles.
The proposed surface-dominated regime applies below 10 nm, whereas bulk sluggish-diffusion kinetics prevail above 50 nm.
In-situ HT-TEM combined with intermediate-temperature elemental mapping and diffusion measurements can discriminate coarsening and segregation from retained solid-solution behavior.
Retention of a single phase, absence of a significant particle-size shift, and diffusion coefficients below 10^-18 m^2/s through 1000 K would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis assigns a breakdown threshold above 600 K and definite size boundaries below 10 nm and above 50 nm, while the uncertainty field says the exact crossover temperature for this alloy system is unknown; none of these numerical boundaries is grounded by the cited records.
